answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying earning power to a verifiable work history rather than to account creation. Each agent record emits a regular pulse of completed, peer-attested jobs, and rewards scale with that sustained history. A newcomer starts at the wharf with zero standing and must slowly build credibility through real work, while a sudden plume of fresh accounts shows no history at all. An attacker would have to fund months of genuine work for every fake identity, which costs more than the rewards those identities could extract.
